flight.rec.goldberg_aria.name: Bach: Aria from the Goldberg Variations
flight.rec.goldberg_aria.title: Aria
flight.rec.goldberg_aria.note: Thirty variations begin and end with the same quiet aria. This is only the beginning, and it is enough.
flight.rec.credit.goldberg_aria: J. S. Bach, Goldberg Variations BWV 988: Aria. Kimiko Ishizaka, piano (Open Goldberg Variations, 2012). CC0 1.0: no attribution required, credited with thanks.
flight.rec.clair_de_lune.name: Debussy: Clair de lune
flight.rec.clair_de_lune.title: Clair de lune
flight.rec.clair_de_lune.note: Music about moonlight lying on water. From here you can see both the moon and the water.
flight.rec.credit.clair_de_lune: Claude Debussy, Clair de lune. Performed by Laurens Goedhart (2011), via Wikimedia Commons. Licensed CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Trimmed and loudness-normalised.
flight.rec.gymnopedie.name: Satie: Gymnopédie No. 1
flight.rec.gymnopedie.title: Gymnopédie No. 1
flight.rec.gymnopedie.note: Slow and sorrowful, the score says. Slow comes by itself up here: nothing falls.
flight.rec.credit.gymnopedie: "Gymnopedie No. 1" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 3.0 License, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Trimmed and loudness-normalised.
flight.rec.rachmaninoff_andante.name: Rachmaninoff: Concerto No. 1, Andante
flight.rec.rachmaninoff_andante.title: Concerto No. 1. Andante
flight.rec.rachmaninoff_andante.performe: Neal O'Doan, piano; University of Washington Symphony Orchestra, Robert Feist
flight.rec.rachmaninoff_andante.note: Rachmaninoff was eighteen when he wrote this. The horn calls, and the piano takes its time to answer, as if searching for words.
flight.rec.credit.rachmaninoff_andante: Sergei Rachmaninoff, Piano Concerto No. 1, Op. 1: II. Andante. Neal O'Doan, piano; University of Washington Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Robert Feist. Al Goldstein collection (ibiblio.org), via Wikimedia Commons. Licensed CC BY-SA 2.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/); the trimmed, loudness-normalised file is shared under the same licence.
flight.rec.strauss_waltzes.name: Strauss: Waltzes
flight.rec.strauss_waltzes.title: Waltzes
flight.rec.strauss_waltzes.performer: The United States Air Force Strings
flight.rec.strauss_waltzes.note: Ships have waltzed through space in the cinema before. Here you can find out how it really is.
flight.rec.credit.strauss_waltzes: Johann Strauss II, waltz medley. The United States Air Force Strings (USAF Band). Public domain (US government work); credited with thanks.
flight.rec.air_1920.name: Bach: Air, a 1920 recording
flight.rec.air_1920.title: Air
flight.rec.air_1920.performer: Joel Belov, violin; Robert Gayler, piano
flight.rec.air_1920.note: Recorded on a wax cylinder more than a century ago. The violin sounds far off, as if it too were flying home.
flight.rec.credit.air_1920: J. S. Bach, Air from the Orchestral Suite No. 3. Joel Belov, violin; Robert Gayler, piano; 1920 cylinder recording. Transfer: UCSB Cylinder Audio Archive. Public domain; credited with thanks.
flight.rec.japanese_sandman.name: Paul Whiteman: The Japanese Sandman
flight.rec.japanese_sandman.title: The Japanese Sandman
flight.rec.japanese_sandman.note: A 1920 fox trot about a man who trades old days for new dreams. Good for dozing off on the couch.
flight.rec.credit.japanese_sandman: Richard A. Whiting, The Japanese Sandman. Paul Whiteman and His Orchestra, 1920 (acoustic 78 rpm). Public domain; credited with thanks.
flight.rec.floating_clouds.name: Arold Valda: Floating Clouds
flight.rec.floating_clouds.title: Floating Clouds
flight.rec.floating_clouds.note: Slow chords in no hurry to go anywhere. The clouds below are not in sight yet, but they are already there.
flight.rec.credit.floating_clouds: "Floating Clouds (Atmospheric C418 Style)". Music by Arold Valda (OpenGameArt). Licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Trimmed and loudness-normalised.
